title: The image of a base change is the inverse image of the image
statement: Let $f:X\to Z$ and $g:Y\to Z$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme], and let $P$ with morphisms $p:P\to X$, $q:P\to Y$ be a fibre product of $f$ and $g$ [def-pc-fibre-product] (so $f\circ p=g\circ q$). Then for every subset $C$ of the underlying set of $X$ one has $q(p^{-1}(C))=g^{-1}(f(C))$ as subsets of $Y$. In particular ($C=X$) the image of the base change $q:P\to Y$ of $f$ along $g$ is $q(P)=g^{-1}(f(X))$.

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 01S1 (lemma-base-change-surjective, line 1489): for a fibre product square with $p:X_{S'}\to X$, $q:Y_{S'}\to Y$ and base change $f_{S'}$, 'Let $Z$ be a subset of the underlying topological space of $X$. Then $q^{-1}(f(Z))=f_{S'}(p^{-1}(Z))$', by Lemma Tag 0495 (lemma-when-point-maps-to-pair: points $x$, $y$ over the same point come from a point of the fibre product); taking $Z=X$ gives the image clause
